completion_data.completion_summary: Built the universal-summary substrate for the stab fibre check as Büchi's complementation chain transposed to monadic k-types over the Z time axis: a public KTypeSummary/ cluster carrying chain steps 2, 3, 3', 4, 5a and 5b sorry-free on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; a seam interface stating the stab bridge plusStab_iff_seamSummary against a four-field hypothesis bundle whose colours field is the unformalized MSO reduction (discharged nowhere); 11 axiom pins; and two wired evidence probes (the substrate run end to end on a concrete infinite fibre, and E2, the depth-2 stratification probe). No decidability result, no complexity bound, no claim that any stab condition is a k-type-determined target.

memory_candidates.content: Mathlib's unusedFintypeInType/unusedDecidableInType linters fire on any theorem whose [Fintype a] [DecidableEq a] binders are consumed only by the proof (a conclusion like Finite (KType sig k), or an equation between kTypeOf values). In this repo neither class has a disposition row in scripts/warning-budget.txt, so a single emission makes C28 exit 2. When the binders are a plan-pinned signature, keep them and suppress declaration-scoped with a `--` reason comment naming both linters directly above the stacked `set_option ... in` lines (C29/C30). A doc comment cannot sit above the set_option stack: the order is comments, set_options, docstring, declaration.

Lean hashes whole files, so a prose-only docstring edit to a leaf module with a large import cone (e.g. ForMathlib/Combinatorics/InfiniteRamseyPairs.lean) invalidates every downstream .olean. A scoped lake build of the touched roots leaves the rest stale, and scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh (whose probes import FormalSystem) then fails spuriously with an object-file-does-not-exist error. Run the unscoped guarded build (or the harness, whose C1 is one) BEFORE the probe gate whenever a widely imported module was touched.

The line-prefix axiom census (grep for lines starting with the word axiom) matches docstring prose: a wrapped sentence whose continuation line begins with the word axiom counts as a declaration (two pre-existing test files and two READMEs already produce such hits). Before reading a count increase as a regression, grep the hits with context and compare against git grep at the baseline commit; a prose hit is fixed by rewrapping the line.
